bluf: Juneteenth weekend Saturday — strong event slate with Nate Bargatze at Moody Center (~12,000, 3 PM), Kevin Morby at Stubb's Outdoor (~2,000, 7 PM), and late-night shows near property. Overnight storms moved through (isolated flash flood risk south of I-10/US-90 corridor). 20–40% residual storm chance this afternoon/evening — brief intense cells possible. Heat index up to 100°F along I-35. US-Iran talks ON: Witkoff and Araghchi both headed to Switzerland — talks resuming Saturday. Lebanon-Hezbollah ceasefire in effect. E. Riverside robbery-homicide suspect remains at large.

incidents.title: Robbery-Homicide — E. Riverside AutoZone (SUSPECT AT LARGE)
incidents.detail: Suspect wanted in fatal shooting of Jose Salgado-Amador, 28, during a robbery at the E. Riverside AutoZone parking lot. APD released new video June 18. Suspect: Hispanic male, 15–20, gray hoodie, light-colored sedan. Austin's 27th homicide of 2026. Unidentified, at large. $1,000 reward active. Case remains open. Brief ALL exterior, valet, and bellstand staff. Suspect demonstrated lethal-force willingness in a robbery context. Report suspicious loitering to APD (512) 974-5000 or Crime Stoppers (512) 472-8477.

incidents.title: Overnight Flash Flooding — South of Austin (I-10/US-90 Corridor)
incidents.location: I-10 / US-90 corridor south of Austin (San Antonio area)
incidents.detail: NWS Austin/San Antonio issued flash flood statements overnight for areas along and south of the I-10/US-90 corridor. Heavy rainfall rates of 2–3 inches/hour possible. Backbuilding convection pushed through Austin's area pre-dawn with lightning. Some isolated flooding possible. Austin proper received storms early morning but greatest flood risk remained to the south toward San Antonio. Residual moisture and 20–40% afternoon storm chance remains. Ensure loading dock drains are clear from overnight rain. Brief valet on wet-weather protocols. Staff commuting from south of Austin (I-35 S or US-183 S) should check roads.

incidents.title: US–Iran Burgenstock Talks RESUMING Saturday
incidents.detail: US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff and Iranian FM Abbas Araghchi are both travelling to Switzerland Saturday for resumption of implementation talks. Israel-Hezbollah ceasefire took effect 4 PM Lebanon time Friday (brokered by US, Qatar, and Iran). Talks had been postponed Thursday amid fighting; ceasefire stabilized them. Next formal round scheduled June 23–25 in Washington, DC. Strait of Hormuz remains open, Iranian oil waivers active. Iran: 'No urgency but meeting planned in coming days.' Situation stabilizing. Positive development — reduced domestic protest risk compared to Friday. Civil unrest threat returns to LOW. Maintain standard posture. No credible threat to property.

incidents.title: SE Austin Homicide Cluster — Cases Ongoing
incidents.detail: Three homicides in SE Austin June 15–17 remain under APD investigation. Francesca Ortiz (Waters at Bluff Springs), husband-wife double homicide (Old Manor Rd), and AutoZone robbery-homicide (E. Riverside). No new SE Austin homicide incidents overnight. APD investigations ongoing — no suspects identified in two of three cases. No direct threat to property. SE I-35 corridor awareness for commuting staff.

civil_unrest.title: Juneteenth Weekend — Continued Activity East Austin
civil_unrest.detail: Juneteenth weekend continues. Saturday events include The Carver Kickback: Juneteenth Edition at the George Washington Carver Museum (1165 Angelina St, East Austin). Beyond the Petal exhibit at Old Bakery and Emporium (1006 Congress Ave — 0.4 mi from property). City services, courts, libraries remain closed Saturday in many areas as weekend holiday observance continues. Foot traffic in East Austin and along Congress Ave elevated compared to a normal Saturday.

civil_unrest.title: US–Iran Protest Watch — REDUCED
civil_unrest.detail: Israel-Hezbollah ceasefire took effect Friday. US-Iran implementation talks resuming in Switzerland Saturday. Domestic protest risk significantly reduced from Friday's ELEVATED status. Monitor social media for any residual demonstration activity near Capitol — unlikely given diplomatic progress. Standard posture.

notes: Overnight/early-morning storms moved through Austin with lightning and locally heavy rain. Greatest flood risk was along and south of I-10/US-90 corridor (San Antonio area). Austin received pre-dawn convection — isolated flooding possible in low-lying areas.

Today: lingering 20–40% chance of isolated-to-scattered afternoon/evening storms. NWS EWX: 'Enough instability could establish with daytime heating where isolated to scattered shower and storm activity will be possible from the afternoon into the night.' Storms capable of heavy rain, localized flooding, frequent lightning.
Heat index values could reach 100°F along the I-35 corridor this afternoon. No heat advisory in effect — below heat advisory threshold.
Outdoor events at risk: Kevin Morby at Stubb's Outdoor (7 PM) — outdoor venue. Monitor NWS EWX for any pre-show cell development 4–6 PM.
Sunday (Father's Day): Drying trend begins. 10–20% storm chance morning only. High near 91°F. Mostly sunny afternoon.
Monday onward: Dry, hot pattern returning. Highs climbing to mid-90s then potentially 103°F by mid-week. Monitor for Heat Advisory issuance Monday or Tuesday.
Deep Eddy Pool CLOSED (permanent closure). Ramsey, Murchison, Barton Springs pools currently closed. Hotel pool remains at elevated demand from guests.

events.name: Nate Bargatze — Moody Center ATX
events.venue: Moody Center ATX, 2001 Robert Dedman Dr
events.detail: Major comedy/entertainment show at Moody Center — sold-out or near-sold-out. ~12,000 attendees. Matinee start at 3 PM — traffic impact on Guadalupe, Red River, and MLK from 1:30 PM. Rideshare surge expected. Show likely ends 5–5:30 PM, driving heavy post-show foot traffic into downtown and 6th Street corridor for dinner and evening entertainment. Some Bargatze attendees will seek Four Seasons bar/restaurant for pre- or post-show experience.

events.name: Kevin Morby — Stubb's Outdoor Amphitheatre
events.detail: Indie rock show at Stubb's outdoor amphitheater, 0.5 mi NE of property. ~2,000 capacity outdoor venue. Outdoor show — monitor afternoon storm potential. If storms develop 3–6 PM, show may face delay or early crowd dispersal. Foot traffic on Red River St and 6th elevated 6–11 PM. High foot traffic overlap with post-Bargatze crowd heading into the evening district.

events.name: Parker Millsap — Antone's Nightclub
events.detail: High-profile Americana show at Antone's, 0.2 mi west of property on 5th Street. Foot traffic on 5th and Lavaca elevated 7–11 PM. Post-show crowd (10:30–midnight) likely to spill toward property entrance on Cesar Chavez. Pre-position exterior staff.

events.name: Franky Wah — Kingdom
events.detail: Electronic music show at Kingdom nightclub on E. 7th St. Late-night crowd — arrivals 10 PM–midnight. E. 7th Street / Red River corridor elevated late night through 2 AM. Standard late-night awareness.

events.venue: The Concourse Project, 10110 N. Lamar Blvd
events.detail: Electronic music show at the Concourse Project, north of downtown. No direct impact to property area. I-35 N northbound traffic elevated post-show (midnight+).

events.crowd: Moderate | Multiple (1 PM / 4 PM / 8 PM CDT)
events.detail: June 20 WC Day 10: Netherlands vs. Sweden (1 PM CDT, Houston NRG); Germany vs. Ivory Coast (4 PM CDT, Toronto); Ecuador vs. Curaçao (8 PM CDT). events.detail: Juneteenth weekend event at the Carver Museum in East Austin. Community cultural event — low risk profile. Foot traffic in East Austin continues from Friday's parade.

property_actions: NATE BARGATZE — MOODY CENTER (~12,000, 3 PM): Largest crowd of the day arrives at Moody Center at 3 PM. Traffic on Guadalupe, MLK, and Red River will be heavy 1:30–4 PM and again 5–6 PM post-show. Many attendees will transition to downtown for dinner and entertainment. Notify concierge and restaurant management to expect elevated walk-in demand 5–7 PM. Valet should be staffed for elevated afternoon volume.

PARKER MILLSAP — ANTONE'S (0.2 mi W, ~500, 8 PM): High foot traffic on 5th Street and Lavaca from 7–11 PM. Brief exterior and door staff. Expect concert pedestrian spillover. Post-show crowd (10:30 PM–midnight) may approach front entrance area.

AFTERNOON STORM WATCH (20–40% CHANCE): Outdoor venues (Stubb's, Stubb's Jr.) are at risk if a storm cell develops 3–7 PM. Monitor NWS EWX. If severe warning issued, activate weather protocol: shelter guests on outdoor terrace/pool deck, notify F&B to prepare for potential early restaurant surge. Ensure loading dock drains are clear from overnight rainfall.

ROBBERY-HOMICIDE SUSPECT STILL AT LARGE: Brief ALL exterior staff — Hispanic male, 15–20, gray hoodie, light-colored sedan. $1,000 reward. Report suspicious loitering: APD (512) 974-5000 / Crime Stoppers (512) 472-8477.

HEAT INDEX UP TO 100°F: No formal advisory in effect, but heat index will approach 100°F this afternoon. Maintain hydration stations at valet and pool deck. Continue 30-min outdoor staff break rotation. Pool closures citywide mean hotel pool will be at maximum capacity — manage access proactively.

JUNETEENTH WEEKEND — ELEVATED OCCUPANCY: Saturday night is expected to be one of the highest-occupancy nights of the weekend. Brief front desk on anticipated check-in volume. Concierge: brief on tonight's event landscape (Bargatze post-show, Antone's, Stubb's, 6th Street) for guest recommendations.

FIFA WC WATCH PARTIES (1 PM / 4 PM): Netherlands vs. Sweden at 1 PM CDT and Germany vs. Ivory Coast at 4 PM CDT drive mid-afternoon bar activity. Monitor 6th Street crowd levels. Staff bar if viewing coverage is offered.
national_context: US-IRAN TALKS RESUMING SATURDAY: Witkoff (US) and Araghchi (Iran FM) both heading to Burgenstock, Switzerland Saturday per Axios/Japan Times. Israel-Hezbollah ceasefire took effect 4 PM Friday Lebanon time, brokered by US, Qatar, and Iran. Next formal round scheduled June 23–25 in Washington, DC. Strait of Hormuz remains open; Iranian oil waivers active. Iran suspended planned Hormuz transit fees during 60-day window. Situation stabilizing — protest risk significantly reduced from Friday's elevated posture.

FIFA WC DAY 10: Netherlands vs. Sweden (1 PM CDT, Houston NRG); Germany vs. Ivory Coast (4 PM CDT, Toronto); Ecuador vs. Curaçao (8 PM CDT). No Austin Q2 Stadium matches today. Netherlands and Germany are the two most significant watch party draws in Austin today.

TROPICAL STORM ARTHUR REMNANTS: Pushed through SE Texas and western Louisiana Friday. Flood warnings were issued along the upper Texas coast. Arthur's moisture plume is the primary driver of weekend rain chances in central Texas. Drying trend expected Sunday as ridging rebuilds from the west.

HEAT WAVE BUILDING NEXT WEEK: NWS Austin/San Antonio: 'A building trend of intense, humid heat is expected across South-Central Texas.' Highs climbing from low 90s up to 103°F by mid-week. Heat Advisory watch for Monday–Wednesday. Pool closures citywide mean hotel pool demand will increase significantly Monday onward.

KARMELO ANTHONY TRIAL EVIDENCE RELEASED: Collin County court released trial evidence Friday (videos, photos, body cam) from the murder trial of Karmelo Anthony, sentenced to 35 years in prison for stabbing 17-year-old Austin Metcalf at a Frisco track meet in 2025. National media coverage renewed. No direct Austin threat; racially charged national narrative may generate protest activity at some Texas venues — low probability for Austin at this time.
lookaheads: SUN Jun 21 — Father's Day + Summer Solstice

High near 91°F. 10–20% storm chance morning only; clears by afternoon. Father's Day — elevated F&B covers for Sunday brunch and dinner. Expect peak reservation demand. 5 Seconds of Summer at Moody Center (8 PM, ~12,000) — major evening crowd on Guadalupe/Red River. Brief staff on event impact.
MON Jun 22 — Heat Wave Ramps Up

High near 95°F. Deep Eddy Pool closed — hotel pool sees sharply elevated demand. Mostly dry. Heat Advisory possible if indices reach 108°F+. Activate heat mitigation protocols for outdoor staff and pool deck.
TUE–WED Jun 23–24 — Peak Heat / US-Iran Washington Talks
Highs approaching 103°F mid-week. NWS monitoring for Heat Advisory. US-Iran formal negotiations scheduled June 23–25 in Washington DC — monitor for protest activity nationally; Austin risk LOW.

First formal implementation round, Washington DC. Topics: nuclear enrichment disposition, final deal framework. Any breakdown could reignite protest activity. Strait of Hormuz remains open through 60-day window regardless.
